title: Linking Issues to Code — Branches, PRs, and Auto-Close
learning_objectives: Create feature branches named with issue numbers for traceability
Use closing keywords in PRs to auto-close issues on merge
See an issue move from In Progress to Done automatically via board automation
Understand the full loop: issue → branch → commits → PR → merge → closed issue
outline: Branch naming conventions that reference issues: feat/42-add-task-list
How GitHub Projects automation works: PR merged → issue closed → card moves to Done
Configuring the automation: setting up the workflow in GitHub Projects
The full loop demonstrated: open issue → branch → commits → PR → merge → Done
Hands-on: Pick one issue from the board, create a branch, make a small commit, open PR, merge, watch the board update

helm_context.feature: Automated issue lifecycle tied to code in Helm
helm_context.deliverable: One issue moved from Backlog → In Progress → Done via actual code merge

criteria: PR uses Closes #N to link the issue
After merge, the issue is automatically closed and the board card moves to Done
Can explain why this automation matters for maintaining an accurate backlog

professor_constraints: Use a real (small) Helm change for the hands-on — don't use a dummy commit
Walk through the automation setup step by step — it's easy to miss
This lesson ties together P01-M03 and P01-M04 — reinforce the full workflow
